slides.title: Which of the following activities should the nurse delegate to the unlicensed as
text: Question: Which of the following activities should the nurse delegate to the unlicensed assistant personnel(UAP)? Select all that apply.
A. Take vital signs on a new admission.
B. Assist with the narcotic count.
C. Check the crash cart for necessary supplies.
D. Administer a tap water enema.
E. Obtain client finger sticks on diabetic clients.
F. Demonstrate how to use an incentive spirometry.
Correct answers: D. Administer a tap water enema.; E. Obtain client finger sticks on diabetic clients.
Topic: Prioritization & Delegation
notes: Rationale:
Correct:
• “Administer a tap water enema” – There are no medications or electrolytes in the enema.
• “Obtain client finger sticks on diabetic clients” – This is in their scope of practice.
Not correct:
• “Take vital signs on a new admission” – Only RNs assess new admissions.
• “Assist with the narcotic count” – Only nurse can do this.
• “Check the crash cart for necessary supplies” – Only nurse can do this.
• “Demonstrate how to use an incentive spirometry” – They can not teach.
(From your class slides.)

slides.title: Which of the following clinical situations should be viewed as an assault?
text: Question: Which of the following clinical situations should be viewed as an assault?
A. The nurse threatens to apply restraints to a client who is exhibiting aggressive behavior.
B. The client requests a medical discharge, but the nurse physically forces the client to stay.
C. The charge nurse sends an email to a staff member which includes a poor performance evaluation about another person.
D. The nurse overhears the primary health care provider making derogatory remarks to the client about the nurse's level of competency.
Correct answer: A. The nurse threatens to apply restraints to a client who is exhibiting aggressive behavior.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:
Correct: “The nurse threatens to apply restraints to a client who is exhibiting…” – Assault is a threat to harm.
Not correct:
• “The client requests a medical discharge, but the nurse physically for…” – This would be battery.
• “The charge nurse sends an email to a staff member which includes a po…” – This would be inappropriate and violate the staff members rights.
• “The nurse overhears the primary health care provider making derogator…” – This would be defamation.

text: Question: Which of the following actions by the nurse demonstrate ethical practice? Select all that apply
A. Notifies PHCP about a client refusing dialysis and wants to stop.
B. Educates client about use and benefits of incentive spirometry when refusing to use device.
C. Refuses to stay overnight on a mandated shift due to fatigue, leaves at the end of current scheduled shift.
D. Confronts a coworker who took narcotics out of a client's medication bin for personal use and takes no further action.
E. Asks a client to “take a walk down the hall so their roommate can speak with the PHCP privately about their biopsy results.”
F. Tells a client they will find out an answer for them.

Correct answers: A. Notifies PHCP about a client refusing dialysis and wants to stop.; B. Educates client about use and benefits of incentive spirometry when refusing to use device.; F. Tells a client they will find out an answer for them.

slides.title: The nurse is caring for a multiple gunshot victim. Which of the following action
text: Question: The nurse is caring for a multiple gunshot victim. Which of the following actions should the nurse take to properly secure and handle legal evidence? Select all that apply.
A. Place bags on the hands and feet.
B. Give clothing and wallet to the family.
C. Cut clothing along the seams, avoiding bullet holes.
D. Collect all personal items, including items from clothing pockets.
E. Place wet clothing and personal belongings in a labeled, sealed plastic bag.
F. Do not allow family members, significant others, or friends to be alone with the client.

Correct answers: A. Place bags on the hands and feet.; C. Cut clothing along the seams, avoiding bullet holes.; D. Collect all personal items, including items from clothing pockets.; F. Do not allow family members, significant others, or friends to be alone with the client.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:
Correct:
• Place paper bags on the hands and feet. Yes, need to preserve evidence.
• “Cut clothing along the seams, avoiding bullet holes.” – Yes, forensics will need to test the bullet hole areas.
• “Collect all personal items, including items from clothing pockets.” – Yes, it will all need listed for potential evidence.
• “Do not allow family members, significant others, or friends to be alone with the client.” – Yes, they could tamper with evidence.
Not correct:
• “Give clothing and wallet to the family.” – No, this might be needed for evidence in future.
• “Place wet clothing and personal belongings in a labeled, sealed plastic bag.” – No, this could harm the evidence if placed with wet items. They should be placed separately, labeled, and sealed.

slides.title: The nurse is caring for a client who asks the nurse to witness an advance direct
text: Question: The nurse is caring for a client who asks the nurse to witness an advance directive. Which of the following actions should the nurse to implement?
A. Decline the client’s request politely.
B. Agree to sign the document as a witness.
C. Notify the PHCP of the client's request.
D. Help the client locate an unrelated third party.
Correct answer: D. Help the client locate an unrelated third party.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:
Correct:
• “Help the client locate an unrelated third party.” – Correct. Two unrelated people witness the signature and sign the document, nurse cannot sign or family member. It's a conflict of interest.
Not correct:
• Decline the clients request politely. Does not help the client.
• “Agree to sign the document as a witness.” – Illegal.
• “Notify the PHCP of the client's request.” – Not the best intervention.
(Copied from the class slide answer page: live review rn management of care s, slide 4.)

slides.title: The nurse needs to witness the signature on informed consent forms for multiple
text: Question: The nurse needs to witness the signature on informed consent forms for multiple clients. Which of the following clients are legally able to sign a consent form for surgery? Select all that apply.
A. 16-year-old married client scheduled for a C-Section.
B. 59-year-old client who speaks Spanish only.
C. 30-year-old client who just received amoxicillin.
D. 88-year-old client who is blind but alert and oriented.
E. 17-year-old client who needs emergency appendectomy.
Correct answers: A. 16-year-old married client scheduled for a C-Section.; C. 30-year-old client who just received amoxicillin.; D. 88-year-old client who is blind but alert and oriented.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:
Correct:
• 16-year-old married client – an emancipated minor (married under 18) can consent.
• 30-year-old who received amoxicillin – an antibiotic does not impair the ability to give consent.
• 88-year-old who is blind but alert and oriented – a disability that does not affect comprehension does not remove the right to sign.
Not correct:
• Spanish-only speaker – needs an interpreter before consent is informed.
• 17-year-old needing an appendectomy – a minor who is not emancipated needs a parent or guardian (emergencies may proceed under implied consent).
(From your class slides.)

slides.title: The nurse is discussing living wills with a client. The client asks the nurse if
text: Question: The nurse is discussing living wills with a client. The client asks the nurse if a living will, prepared 3 years ago, remains in effect. Which response should the nurse provide to the client?
A. “Yes, a living will never expire.”
B. “You need to speak to an attorney.”
C. “I will call someone to answer your question.”
D. It is recommended to review them yearly and update with your health care provider.”
Correct answer: D. It is recommended to review them yearly and update with your health care provider.”
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:
Correct:
• “It is recommended to review them yearly and update with your health care provider.” – Yes, it is recommended to review them yearly and update with the health care provider.
Not correct:
• “Yes, a living will never expire.” – Not the best answer.
• “You need to speak to an attorney.” – An attorney does not have to complete an advance directive.
• “I will call someone to answer your question.” – This does not provide the client with help. “

text: Question: The nurse is teaching nursing staff about computerized documentation. Which of the following information should the nurse include ?
A. Document pain findings within the hour of assessment.
B. Promote care continuity by using standardized care plans.
C. Omit narrative progress notes for clinical condition changes.
D. Use predefined statements for abnormal findings while charting by exception.
Correct answer: B. Promote care continuity by using standardized care plans.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:

Electronic records support continuity of care through standardized care plans that every discipline can see. Charting by exception uses predefined statements for NORMAL findings, and abnormal findings and condition changes still require narrative notes, so the other options are wrong.
